cards.name: Boltz-2
cards.tagline: fold a sequence, or co-fold a complex
cards.note: One sequence folds one structure, for a target card to take. Fill in a second sequence and the two are folded together as a complex - a receptor with the DNA, RNA or peptide that binds it - which goes on to be prepared and simulated. A structure of more chains than three is a job for the Boltz-2 page.

settings.label: Sequence
settings.why: one chain, in one-letter codes. Case does not matter - neither tool makes the distinction, so a sequence pasted in lower case is read as upper - but a letter that is not a residue does, and is refused here rather than folded as nothing

settings.label: What it is
settings.why: the alphabet the sequence is checked against, and the model used for it

settings.label: Copies
settings.why: more than one folds a homo-oligomer: the same sequence again as chains A, B, C

settings.label: Sequence of the second chain
settings.why: fill this in to fold a complex rather than one chain: the two are folded together, in the order of the boxes, and what comes out is a complex

settings.label: What the second one is
settings.why: the alphabet it is checked against, and the model used for it

settings.label: Sequence of the third chain

cards.name: Prepare
cards.tagline: prepare the receptor and the partner each on its own, then rejoin them
cards.note: Put in by the canvas on every link that carries a structure into a docking card or the simulation, and part of that link rather than a card of its own: it splits what arrives into the receptor and the partner, prepares each on its own - protonation at the pH above, termini, disulfides, gaps - puts them back together and checks the net charge. A side of several chains is prepared whole, so the bonds between its chains are kept. Into a docking card the waters and hetero groups are dropped, except the ions that docking can use. What it decided is listed on the card when it has run.

settings.label: pH
settings.why: every molecule is protonated at this pH, and one flow has one pH

notes.propka: pdb2pqr with propka at the pH above: each titratable residue gets the state its own surroundings call for
notes.pdbfixer: PDBFixer's rules at the pH above, which are the standard states and no more
notes.none: the hydrogens in the file, or the engine's own defaults where there are none

settings.label: Longest gap to model, residues
settings.why: a gap inside a chain up to this long, found from the sequence the file records, is built, relaxed and its joins checked, as ADCP builds one; a longer one is left open and its two ends capped (Cap the breaks). 12 at most, 0 builds none, and a chain's missing ends are never built

settings.label: Trim predicted tails below pLDDT
settings.why: for a predicted model: terminal residues under this confidence are trimmed; 0 keeps every one, and a structure with no pLDDT in it is untouched

settings.label: Alternate location to keep
settings.why: a crystal structure that models two positions for a side chain keeps this one; the atoms of the others are dropped

settings.label: Model to take
settings.why: for an NMR ensemble or any multi-model file: which model is prepared. The first unless you say otherwise

settings.label: Crystal waters
settings.why: for the simulation; into a docking card every water is dropped

notes.far: keep those within 5 Å of the partner

settings.label: Keep metals and cofactors
settings.why: into the simulation they ride through at their own coordinates, and it decides which side of the interface each belongs to; into a docking card only the ions that docking can use are kept, and the rest are listed as dropped

settings.label: Drop the crystallisation buffers
settings.why: glycerol, sulfate, PEG, acetate, DMSO and the rest of what the crystallographer added; off, each one has to be covered by a force field or the run is refused by name

settings.label: Keep the hetero groups that are neither
settings.why: a group that is not a buffer, a metal or a known cofactor: kept only if a force field here covers it, and named in the refusal if not

settings.label: Also drop, by residue name
settings.why: residue names dropped whatever their class, separated by commas: NAD, HEM. This is what a refusal naming a group it cannot cover asks for

settings.label: Cap the breaks
settings.why: a gap left open has its two ends capped, an NME on the residue before it and an ACE on the residue after it, so neither is a charged terminus the protein does not have; the chain's own termini stay charged. Off, each piece ends in charged termini, an OXT before the gap and NH3+ after it

settings.why: under 5 Å the head groups see their own image, over 40 Å is water for nothing

water.why: not read: the run is in a water box

settings.label: Bilayer centre along z, Å
settings.why: where the middle of the bilayer sits; 0 is the OPM convention and what an oriented structure expects

water.why: not read: the run is in a water box

notes.as_imported: the structure's membrane normal is already z, as an OPM file's is. A folded or docked model is not: say its segments below, or orient it before the flow
notes.opm: fetch the OPM orientation, which needs the internet and so a login node
notes.annotation: orient on the transmembrane segments, from the ones typed below or the ones UniProt annotates

water.why: not read: the run is in a water box

settings.label: Transmembrane segments
settings.why: as chain:start-end, separated by commas: A:30-56, A:71-96. Typed ones are used in place of whatever was found

water.why: not read: the run is in a water box

notes.compact: a truncated octahedron: the fewest waters for the same minimum image distance, and the default
notes.cubic: a cube, for comparison with work that used one
notes.rectangular: an orthorhombic box, which is what a bilayer takes

desmond.why: Desmond's System Builder builds an orthorhombic box whatever is asked

membrane.why: a bilayer is periodic in x and y, so the box is rectangular

settings.label: Padding, Å
settings.why: water between the solute and the box edge; under the 10 Å cutoff the complex sees its own periodic image

membrane.why: not read: a bilayer's water is the padding above and below it

settings.label: Salt
settings.why: the box is neutralised first, then brought to the concentration below

notes.KCl: for work done in potassium buffer
notes.MgCl2: for a nucleic acid, which binds Mg2+; not for a bilayer, which takes a monovalent pair

membrane.why: a bilayer build places a monovalent pair: NaCl or KCl

settings.label: Salt concentration, mM
settings.why: 150 mM is physiological. It is also the salt MM-GBSA is computed at, so it changes the binding energy as well as the box

settings.label: Residues held still in production
settings.why: as 54,56,66-70 or A54,B12-16, in the numbering the preparation kept. For a run meant to answer what the rest does while these stay put
settings.placeholder: nothing is held: the whole complex is free

settings.label: Production restraint, kcal/mol/Å²
settings.why: how hard those residues are held, and the first rung of the equilibration ladder either way

cases.why: the first rung of the equilibration ladder; no residue is held in production

settings.label: Score from, ns
settings.why: skip the start, where the complex is still settling; 0 scores from the first frame

settings.label: Score to, ns
settings.why: empty scores to the end

settings.label: Score every, ps
settings.why: how often a frame of that window is scored; it can be no finer than the interval the frames above are kept at

settings.label: Write each run's report when it finishes
settings.why: the run's own report, as the Runs screen would write it: one job per run, behind the simulation

settings.label: Make each run's videos when it finishes
settings.why: a job of its own per run, cut from the trajectory

settings.label: Tidy each run when it finishes
settings.why: a last job packs away the small files a finished run no longer needs; the results still load. Off, a batch of runs is a great many files

settings.label: Frames the viewer shows, one in
settings.why: the trajectory the Results viewer loads is thinned by this, so 20 of the 5000 frames kept is 250 to scrub through

settings.label: Temperature, K
settings.why: the thermostat's target through heating, equilibration and production

settings.label: Pressure, bar
settings.why: the barostat's target once the box is equilibrated at constant pressure

settings.label: Timestep, fs
settings.why: 2 fs, or 4 fs with hydrogen mass repartitioning

desmond.why: Desmond runs its RESPA scheme: the timestep is fixed at 2 fs and there is no hydrogen mass repartitioning

settings.label: Equilibration, ps
settings.why: over the restraint ladder

settings.label: Heating, ps
settings.why: from 0 K to the temperature above, restrained, before the ladder

settings.label: Minimisation steps
settings.why: on the built box, before any heating: it takes the clashes out of the solvation

settings.label: Random seed
settings.why: -1 lets each replicate pick its own

settings.label: Water
settings.why: empty takes what the force field was fitted to

notes: the force field's own pairing: OPC with ff19SB, TIP3P with ff14SB, SPC with Desmond's OPLS
notes.OPC: ff19SB's own, and not for NAMD or Desmond
notes.TIP4P-Ew: not for NAMD, which cannot run a four-site water from the Amber topology

membrane.why: a bilayer build has one water and it is written for you: TIP3P, or SPC on Desmond, whose lipid patches come hydrated with it

settings.label: Protein force field
settings.why: empty takes the engine's own: ff19SB on the four Amber-topology engines, OPLS_2005 on Desmond

notes.ff14SB: the same four, for comparison with older work
notes.OPLS_2005: Desmond, which types the whole system with its own OPLS

desmond.why: Desmond types the whole system with its own OPLS: OPLS_2005 or OPLS4

membrane.why: a bilayer build has one force field and it is written for you: ff14SB, which is the only one OpenMM ships lipid17 alongside, or Desmond's own OPLS

settings.label: DNA and RNA force field
settings.why: for a strand in the run; empty takes the engine's usual

notes.bsc1+OL3: any engine but Desmond, which types DNA and RNA with its own OPLS and takes no choice

notes.gpu: one card per replicate, which is how these engines are meant to be run
notes.cpu: one whole node, for a short check while the GPU queue is full: Amber or GROMACS, at most 10 ns and 500 frames

settings.label: GPU type
settings.why: empty takes the cluster's usual card

notes: the cluster's default, which on Grace is a100
notes.auto: the fastest type with a free card at submit, which is what keeps a run out of the a100 queue when a40s are idle
notes.a100: 40 GB, the fastest here and the default
notes.a40: 48 GB, on its own partition and often free

cpu.why: not read: the run is on CPU

settings.label: GPUs per replicate
settings.why: one is what Amber, OpenMM and Desmond each run a replicate on, however many are asked for; NAMD uses them all

a100.why: a Grace a100 node has 2 cards

a40.why: a Grace a40 node has 3 cards

rtx.why: a Grace rtx node has 2 cards

t4.why: a Grace t4 node has 4 cards

cpu.why: not read: the run is on CPU

settings.label: CPU cores per replicate
settings.why: beside the card, for the parts that are not on it; a CPU check takes a whole node whatever this says

settings.label: Memory per replicate, GB
settings.why: Grace refuses a job that asks for none; raise it for a system of many hundreds of thousands of atoms

settings.label: Replicates running at once
settings.why: a throttle for a batch of runs against one allocation: empty queues them all and lets the cluster decide

settings.label: Walltime
settings.why: left empty, the simulation works one out from the length, the replicates and the size of the system, which is the number to beat. A typed one is each production job's limit, so a shorter one cuts a long run into more segments

settings.label: Partition
settings.why: empty takes the partition the GPU type lives on, which is what you want unless you are aiming at a reservation
settings.placeholder: the one that carries the card

settings.label: Account to charge
settings.why: the Slurm account every job of every run is charged to, the preparation included
settings.placeholder: whatever you are charged by default
